topics.topic: Canonical host/authority form for Host header and request_digest hashing (case, default port, IPv6 brackets, IDN/punycode)
questions: How is the `host` header value derived exactly (default port included or omitted, IPv6 bracket form, IDN/punycode handling), so that `request_digest` is deterministic and stable across restarts/clients?
What exact canonical form of URL authority/host header is hashed in `request_digest` (case of host, default port inclusion, punycode/IDNA form), so approval matching is stable and deterministic?

quotes: The request an approval covers is described, before sending, by: the method; the full URL with its query (A09 rules 1 and 2); every header sent on the wire, names lower-cased and in code-point order, each with its value, except that the credential header and `content-length` appear by name only — the length follows from the body described — and the `multipart/form-data` content type without its `boundary` parameter.

The URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path, which must start with one `/` and contain no `//`, no `.` or `..` segment, no `?` or `#`, and no scheme or host; a path that does not is not invocable (A08 rule 3). Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.
judgement.divergence: Behavior A: derive `host`/URL authority exactly from configured `api_base_url` text (e.g., preserve case, omit default port, keep Unicode host form); Behavior B: canonicalize authority (e.g., lowercase host, punycode IDN, and/or include default port). The owner notices because approval reuse versus re-ask changes when `request_digest` matches, and the external service may notice different `Host` values for routing.
judgement.why: The rules require hashing the full URL and header values but do not fix one canonical authority/Host value form, so careful implementations can produce different request digests and wire requests.

topics.topic: Classification of non-standard/out-of-range HTTP status codes for read vs non-read outcomes
questions: How must statuses outside these classes (for example `600` or another non-standard parsed status) be classified for `read` and non-`read` operations?

topics.topic: Handling required_headers that collide with kernel-generated headers (refuse vs duplicates/precedence)
questions: If `required_headers` contains a header name that the kernel also sets (`host`, `accept-encoding`, `content-type`, `content-length`), is that request refused, or are duplicate/conflicting values sent, and if sent which value wins?

topics.topic: How invalid required-header syntax is classified (manifest mismatch vs pre-send failure vs transport mapping)
questions: How must the kernel classify invalid required-header syntax (for example illegal header name characters or control characters in values): manifest mismatch at proposal/accept, pre-send `operation_failed`, or transport-level outcome mapping?

topics.topic: Required external behavior when runtime symlink detection occurs during run-advancing store calls
questions: When this happens inside a request that is advancing a run, what external behavior is required: return an internal refusal only, stop the kernel process, or force affected runs to terminal status?

topics.topic: Validation behavior when manifest service/capabilities fields have wrong JSON types
questions: What is the exact behavior when `service`/`capabilities` exist but are the wrong JSON types (for example `capabilities` is not a list, entries are not objects, or required fields are non-strings)?

topics.topic: Whether NodeExecution.executed is populated when a receiving-node contract_violation occurs before execution starts
questions: For a receiving-node `contract_violation` raised before node execution starts, must `NodeExecution.executed` still name the implementation/binding, or be absent because nothing ran?

topics.topic: Whether api_base_url may include path/query/fragment and how it is joined to request URLs
questions: Must `api_base_url` with a path/query/fragment be refused, or allowed and concatenated literally?
